text: When the sea suddenly pulls back... don't watch. Run.
You may have ten minutes left... or less.
You're at the beach. It's sunny. Everyone's happy.
Then the water pulls back. Sand, fish, and coral appear out of nowhere.
People walk out to grab the fish. They start filming.
That's the biggest mistake you can make.
In 2004, this is exactly what happened. More than two hundred thirty thousand people died.
Out in the open ocean, the wave moves as fast as a jet plane.
And near the shore, it's still faster than anyone can run.
Rule one. Leave your things. All of them.
Rule two. Go up. Thirty meters high, or three kilometers inland.
No hill? Get to the third floor of a strong concrete building.
Rule four. Never go back after the first wave. The next one is often bigger.
In 2004, a ten-year-old girl noticed the sea pulling back. She had learned it in school.
She screamed. And almost one hundred people survived because of her.
And it has happened here. In 1976, thousands died in a tsunami in the Moro Gulf, in the Philippines.
